name: court
notes: plain open ground; no cost basis stated in docs, defaulted to 1

name: the span, one tile
notes: width-1 chokepoint per Bel-Iddin's note; that's a grid-topology fact, not a cost -- this table only carries cost

name: high terrace
notes: riding impassable per Tasme ('cannot climb the terraces'); +1 wet per map_f00's terrain note ('stepped terraces (+1 cost when wet)'), applied here to infantry/armor -- unclear if a riding-wet cost is even meaningful given riding is already blocked outright

name: wall face / temple (impassable)
notes: labelled impassable in both map_f00.txt and map_f00_reference.png legends; flying=1 is my inference (open air above a retaining wall), not stated outright

name: the wall (destructible structure)
notes: impassable while standing; Enmet removes it turn 1 (prologue_structures.str_wall). This table has no state machine -- treat as ter_court once destroyed. Needs real structure-state wiring later, not just a static lookup

name: planted terrace
notes: no cost stated anywhere in the docs; defaulted to 1, revise if this should slow movement

name: stair
notes: no cost stated anywhere in the docs; defaulted to 1. These are the only gaps through the x rows -- worth deciding if they should be slower or movement-type-restricted

name: the image / statue (structure)
notes: occupies its tile as a structure, not steppable -- same pattern as ter_wall, see prologue_structures.str_statue

name: seize (Sargath only)
notes: functionally plain ground; 'Sargath only' is an objective rule (who may seize), not a movement cost -- out of scope here

name: channel
notes: flying only, per map_f00's own approaches list ('the channels (flying only)'); Sirru's note says water blocks feet but not arrows -- that's an attack-range rule, a separate system, not represented in this table

name: rooftop (map_a02)
notes: flying only, per map_a02's own approaches list ('rooftops (flying)').

name: building (map_a02, impassable)
notes: street-front facades; also blocks flying, unlike f00's wall-face -- these are roofed structures, not a retaining wall's open-air top.

name: wide street (map_a02)
notes: per map_a02's approaches: 'wide street (riding)'. All movement types pay the same cost here -- width, not cost, is what favors riding (no per-map chokepoint-vs-type system exists, same limitation ter_span's note already flags).

name: narrow street (map_a02)
notes: per map_a02's approaches: 'narrow street (foot)' -- armor/riding blocked outright, same convention as ter_terrace_high blocking riding.

name: crowd plaza (map_a02)
notes: map_a02.terrain: 'crowd tiles' -- cost 2 for ground types (congestion), flying unaffected. Where Boyan and the townsfolk stand, and the deploy zone.

name: cloister (map_a03)
notes: map_a03's own approaches: 'cloister (indoors, no cold)'. Blocks flying (roofed corridor) -- the tradeoff for being the only cold-safe terrain here.

name: open ward (map_a03)
notes: map_a03's approaches: 'open ward (fast, costly)' -- 'fast' is the cost-1 move, 'costly' is the hazard_dmg. map_a03.terrain: 'cold drains 2 HP/turn outdoors'.

name: rubble (map_a03)
notes: ruined-priory debris; armor/riding slowed more than infantry, flying unaffected. Still outdoors -- same 2 HP/turn cold drain as ter_open_ward.

name: reliquary (map_a03, objective)
notes: the 'take-or-give' objective tile itself; costs and hazard match ter_open_ward (it sits in the open ward, not the cloister).

name: defend point (map_a02, objective)
notes: same cost as ter_plaza (it IS a plaza tile) -- distinct symbol only so map logic can find the objective without scanning for a specific coordinate.

name: escape tile (map_a03, objective)
notes: same cost/hazard as ter_cloister (it's the ring's south-center tile) -- distinct symbol so map logic can find the objective.

name: ford (map_d03)
notes: per map_d03's own approaches: 'southern ford (foot only)' -- same cost profile as ter_narrow_street, distinct symbol/name since it's a river crossing, not a street.

name: covered arcade / awnings (map_b15)
notes: map_b15.terrain: 'awnings block flight, arcade blocks bows' -- the flight block is modeled (blocks flying like ter_cloister does); the bow-block is an attack-range restriction, not a movement cost, and isn't modeled anywhere yet.
